resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection Permitting Occupancy (For Resale), also called the certificate of habitability or Certificate of Occupancy Compliance
resale_co.issued_by: Hardyston Township Construction Office, acting as the Construction Official for the Borough of Franklin
resale_co.lead_time: The certificate must be granted or denied within 15 days after the written application is received.
requirements: Inspection by the Construction Official (or agent) for compliance with Borough ordinances; the official lists the corrections needed
Smoke alarms on all floors and within 10 feet of all sleeping areas; carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas
Portable fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (checklist still lists it)
GFCI outlets near sinks and in damp locations; cover plates on all receptacles, switches and junction boxes
Sump pumps may not discharge to the town sewer; food disposal grinders are not permitted
Handrails on stairs with three or more risers; guardrails on decks 30 inches or more above grade
Remodeled kitchens, baths and finished basements are checked for permits; open permits must be inspected and approved before the certificate
Attached garage fire-resistive ratings maintained; no basement bedrooms without code egress; no double-keyed deadbolts on the main entrance door
Interior walls, exterior coverings, chimneys and accessory structures (decks, pools, sheds) in good condition and meeting zoning and building codes
If the home converted from oil to gas, the oil tank must have been properly decommissioned

Title may transfer after the application is filed, but no one may move in until all listed corrections are completed; a certificate for closing purposes only (no occupancy) and a temporary certificate (TCO) are options on the form

fees.label: Resale certificate of habitability, first tier (code text reads 'Within 10 business days of occupancy')
Resale, less than 10 but more than 4 business days before occupancy
fees.quote: Less than 10 business days but more than 4 business days of occupancy $85

fees.label: Resale, less than 4 business days before occupancy
fees.quote: Less than 4 business days of occupancy $150

fees.label: Reinspection to abate after the second violation notice, each
fees.quote: Reinspection fee to abate after second violation notice, each $25

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for a Certificate of Inspection Permitting Occupancy (For Resale) from the Hardyston Township website and return it, signed, with payment (checks payable to Hardyston Twp.) to the Hardyston Township Construction Office, 149 Wheatsworth Road, Suite A, Hardyston, NJ 07419. The form asks for the closing date, block and lot, owner and buyer details, and whether the home will be owner occupied or a rental, and lets you choose a full certificate, a certificate for closing purposes only (no occupancy) or a temporary certificate. Review the Certificate of Habitability Check List before the inspection.
resale_co.contact_title: Hardyston Township Building Department (construction office for Franklin Borough)

resale_co.notes: Borough code Section 96-4 (read in full through the ecode360 print view) requires a certificate of habitability inspection permitting occupancy before anyone occupies a dwelling after a transfer of title or a new rental, and makes real estate brokers and agents who take part in a violating transaction liable too. Fees come from Chapter 119; the ecode360 table lists the resale tiers as 'Within 10 business days of occupancy $50', 'Less than 10 business days but more than 4 business days of occupancy $85' and 'Less than 4 business days of occupancy $150'. The first tier's wording is odd (it likely means 10 or more business days); confirm. The fee quotes are typed from the ecode360 table, where the dollar figure sits in a separate cell. The same schedule lists $50 for a rental certificate. The Borough's building page links to the Hardyston page for the application and forms. The checklist still lists a portable fire extinguisher, which the state dropped from the sale smoke certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19); the Borough may still require it locally under its habitability certificate, so confirm.

requirements: Smoke alarms on all floors and within ten feet of all sleeping areas
Carbon monoxide alarms installed and maintained in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas
At least one portable fire extinguisher (2-1/2 to 10 pound, ABC type) within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no more than 5 feet above the floor (form still lists it)

authorities.name: Hardyston Township Construction Office for the Borough of Franklin (smoke/CO checked as part of the resale certificate of habitability); Sussex County Fire Marshal is the fire code enforcing agency
authorities.lead_time: Same as the resale certificate: decided within 15 days of a complete application; fee tiers by business days before occupancy.
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke/CO certificate application for Franklin Borough was found. The Borough's Fire Marshall page says fire inspections are done through Hardyston Township (973-823-7020, follow the prompts to the Construction Department), and the Hardyston checklist for the resale certificate covers smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms and the fire extinguisher. Call the Hardyston Construction Department to confirm whether a separate smoke/CO certificate (and fee) is issued.

evidence.quote: As of October 2010, the Sussex County Fire Marshall provides Fire prevention services for the Borough.

The local enforcing agency shall be the Office of the Fire Marshall for the County of Sussex, which shall hereinafter be known as the local enforcing agency.

fire_cert.notes: Franklin Borough's fire code enforcing agency is the Sussex County Fire Marshal (Borough code Chapter 124 and the NJ DCA LEA registry, code C), but the Sussex County Sheriff's Fire Marshal page lists County smoke detector compliance inspections only for Branchville, Fredon, Green and Newton, and lists Franklin Boro only for fire permits. The NJ DCA fire directory (old survey, 2/1/2019) names the Hardyston Building Dept, (973) 823-7020, as Franklin's smoke detector compliance office, and the Borough's own Fire Marshall page sends fire inspections to Hardyston's Construction Department. So the smoke/CO check appears to be done by the Hardyston Construction Office as part of the resale certificate of habitability, with no separate published smoke/CO fee. County fire official per the directory: Mark Snook, (973) 579-0380, msnook@sussexcountysheriff.com. The checklist still requires a portable fire extinguisher even though P.L.2025, c.19 removed it from the state sale certificate in February 2025.

other_items.label: New water service application on change of ownership
other_items.detail: When ownership changes, the new owner must file a new application for Borough water service; the Public Works Committee may discontinue service until it is filed and approved. Charges continue until written notice of the change or transfer of ownership is given.

other_items.label: Open permits and unpermitted work
other_items.detail: Open permits must be inspected and approved before the certificate of habitability is issued; remodeled kitchens, baths and finished basements are checked for permits, and the owner must obtain any missing permits and inspections.

other_items.label: Sump pump discharge
other_items.detail: Sump pumps cannot discharge into the town sewer; this is checked at the resale inspection.

other_items.label: Oil tank decommissioning
other_items.detail: If the home converted from oil to gas, the inspector asks whether the oil tank was properly decommissioned.

open_questions: Is a separate smoke/CO certificate (CSACMAPFEC) issued for Franklin Borough sales, and by whom (Hardyston Construction Office or the Sussex County Fire Marshal)? Is there a separate fee?
Does the first resale fee tier ($50) apply to applications 10 or more business days before occupancy? The code text says 'Within 10 business days of occupancy'.
Does Franklin still require the portable fire extinguisher at resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
How long is the resale certificate valid, and how far ahead are inspections being scheduled now that inspections have resumed?
